title: 03 Complex numbers: Visual Guide
outline: 1. Circle Becomes Plane | the unit circle from lesson 02 beside the complex plane, with one angle slider and one modulus slider driving both | a complex number is a terminal point that was allowed to change length, so the unit circle is exactly the numbers of modulus 1 and polar form is that bracket with an r in front

2. Distance And Conjugate | two draggable numbers in the plane, switched between distance (with its rise-and-run triangle), midpoint and conjugate reflections | distance is subtract-then-take-modulus and midpoint is the component average, both borrowed unchanged from coordinate geometry, while the conjugate is the reflection that turns a complex denominator real because z times conj z equals a^2 + b^2

3. Modulus And Argument | one point moved by its real and imaginary parts, showing the radius, the swept angle, the quadrant, and atan(b/a) next to the principal argument | modulus is a length that is never negative and never an angle, the principal argument is the representative chosen in (-pi, pi], and atan(b/a) goes exactly pi wrong on the left-hand side because it cannot point leftward at all

4. Multiply By Rotating | two numbers in polar form with sliders for both moduli and arguments, switched between product, quotient and square, drawn as arrows with the arithmetic shown line by line | multiplying multiplies the moduli and adds the arguments (the angle addition identities are the proof), dividing divides and subtracts, and De Moivre raises the modulus to the power while only multiplying the argument

5. Counting Every Root | the roots of three different degree-n polynomials plotted in the plane, with multiplicity badges and dashed conjugate-pair connectors | every nonconstant polynomial has a complex root and a degree-n one has exactly n counting multiplicity, which is not the same as n distinct roots, and real coefficients additionally force nonreal roots to arrive in conjugate pairs
